instruction: Buy one KALLAX Shelf Unit for each of my siblings and parents on Amazon, and have it delivered to their homes. Club purchases for the same place in the same order to save delivery fees.
notes: Siblings and parents (and their home addresses) are discovered at runtime via phone.search_contacts with relationship 'sibling' and 'parent'; the relationship names are domain constants so both lookups can be required before any address/cart action. The problem instantiates a representative configuration of two distinct homes: home-1 shared by two relatives (quantity 2, e.g. both parents) and home-2 with one relative (quantity 1). At runtime, instantiate one home object per distinct home_address across all sibling+parent contacts, with household-size equal to the number of relatives there, and repeat the add_address -> add_product_to_cart(quantity) -> place_order triple once per home; clubbing is enforced because each order is placed from a cart holding exactly the units for one address. The cart is modelled as a single slot: it starts dirty (unknown pre-existing items), amazon.clear_cart empties it, add_product_to_cart fills it for one home and place_order consumes it. Payment card id comes from amazon.show_payment_cards; product id from amazon.search_products. supervisor.complete_task takes the product and the two home records so its precondition equals the goal conjunction; no answer is required.

plan: (amazon-add-address home-1-name home-1-street home-1-city home-1-state home-1-country home-1-zip amazon-token home-1)
(amazon-add-address home-2-name home-2-street home-2-city home-2-state home-2-country home-2-zip amazon-token home-2)
